findings.finding: FINRA's 2021 regulatory notice distinguishes outstanding short-interest positions from executed short-sale activity and states that exchange-listed short-interest reports are supplied to the listing exchange for publication. This is a historical regulatory description, not proof of any present FINRA API's complete coverage.

Nasdaq Trader describes issue-level public query as a rolling 12 months, twice-monthly settlement dates, and release after 4:00 p.m. ET on dissemination dates. Settlement date is not a decision-time publication date.

The SOXX Nasdaq page rendered 'Data is currently not available' in this review, so it supplied no exact 2011-2022 observation or historical first-public timestamp. This does not prove Nasdaq has no underlying records.

Nasdaq Data Link's indexed official product description says its short-interest feed begins at 2022-09-30 settlement, insufficient for the frozen 2011-2022 training calendar on its own. The JavaScript product page did not render its text in this browser tool, so this is an indexed-description observation, not direct exact-byte coverage certification or proof that Nasdaq has no earlier archive.

Nasdaq describes the Short Interest Report as a subscription/SFTP data product; the inspected page does not certify that a 2011-2022 SOXX raw archive and revision vintages are included. No subscription or purchase was made.
